Implement test for JSON pointer: schemaNode with nested property: {"properties":{"name":{"type":"string"}}}. Then getRefSchemaNode("#/properties/name") returns that node.

Test fragment: metaSchema.getNodeByFragmentRef returns node.

Test when node missing leads to handleNullNode: need to simulate fetchSubSchemaNode returning a JsonSchema that has ref node.

Simplify: test getRefSchemaNode returns missing node (null) when not found.

Test findLexicalRoot: create parent schema with hasId false, child with hasId true then findLexicalRoot returns child.

We need to use JsonSchema.from to create child schema.

Potentially we need to make JsonSchemaFactory but not needed.

We'll create a minimal ValidationContext implementation as a mock with necessary methods: getMetaSchema, resolveSchemaId (return null), getURIFactory (return a simple factory that just resolves), newValidator returns mock JsonValidator.

Define mock JsonValidator with methods: validate returns empty set; preloadJsonSchema does nothing; getKeyword? not needed.

Also need ExecutionContext, CollectorContext etc. We can mock ExecutionContext with getCollectorContext returning a new CollectorContext with default config.

Simplify: for validate we can call JsonSchema.validate(rootNode) which internally creates ExecutionContext using createExecutionContext, which uses config from validationContext. We'll provide config mock with necessary methods: isCustomMessageSupported false, doLoadCollectors false, etc.

But ExecutionContext uses CollectorContext constructor requiring booleans; we can instantiate real CollectorContext.

We need to provide config methods: isCustomMessageSupported, isUnevaluatedItemsAnalysisDisabled, isUnevaluatedPropertiesAnalysisDisabled, doLoadCollectors, etc.

We can create a simple Config class implementing necessary methods using a stub class extending SchemaValidatorsConfig.

But SchemaValidatorsConfig is a class (likely with getters/setters). We can instantiate new SchemaValidatorsConfig() and set needed fields via methods (if accessible). For simplicity, we can mock Config using Mockito.

But JsonSchema.createExecutionContext calls validationContext.getConfig() then config.getExecutionContextSupplier etc. So we need config mock with getExecutionContextSupplier returning null and other methods not needed.

Thus we can mock Config.

Implementation steps:

- @RunWith(MockitoJUnitRunner.class)
- @Mock ValidationContext validationContext;
- @Mock JsonMetaSchema metaSchema;
- @Mock SchemaValidatorsConfig config;
- @Mock JsonValidator validator; // for stub

- Set up in @Before: when(validationContext.getMetaSchema()).thenReturn(metaSchema); when(validationContext.getConfig()).thenReturn(config); when(validationContext.resolveSchemaId(any())).thenReturn(null); when(validationContext.getURIFactory()).thenReturn(new URIFactory() { ... })? Actually URIFactory is interface? Not in code snippet. Could be from networknt library. To avoid complexity, we can pass null currentUri to JsonSchema.from and ensure combineCurrentUriWithIds returns null (since id null). That method uses validationContext.resolveSchemaId which returns null, so returns currentUri (null). So we can pass null currentUri.

Thus JsonSchema schema = JsonSchema.from(validationContext, "#", null, schemaNode, null, false);

Need a schemaNode: ObjectMapper mapper = new ObjectMapper(); JsonNode schemaNode = mapper.readTree("{\"type\":\"string\"}");

Also need validationContext.newValidator stub: when(validationContext.newValidator(anyString(), anyString(), any(JsonNode.class), any(JsonSchema.class), anyString())).thenReturn(validator);

Also validator.validate returns empty set.

Now tests:

1. testGetCurrentUriReturnsNullWhenNoUri: assertNull(schema.getCurrentUri());

2. testGetRefSchemaNodeWithJsonPointer: create schemaNode with nested property. Use schemaNode = mapper.readTree("{\"properties\":{\"name\":{\"type\":\"string\"}}}"); then getRefSchemaNode("#/properties/name") should return node with type "string". Since findAncestor returns itself (parent null). In method, jsonPointer starts with "#/", then jsonPointer = ref.substring(1) => "/properties/name". Then URL decode and node = node.at(jsonPointer). At should return the nested node. So test.

3. testGetRefSchemaNodeWithFragment: mock metaSchema.getNodeByFragmentRef to return a node. Set when(metaSchema.getNodeByFragmentRef(anyString(), any(JsonNode.class))).thenReturn(fragmentNode). Then call getRefSchemaNode("#/definitions/foo")? Actually fragment pattern is starts with "#" and length>1. Provide ref "#/defs". We'll create fragmentNode = mapper.readTree("{\"def\":\"value\"}"); test that method returns that node.

4. testFindLexicalRoot: create parent schema with hasId false, child schema with hasId true. To set hasId true we need schemaNode having id keyword. MetaSchema.getIdKeyword returns something like "$id". We can mock metaSchema.getIdKeyword() to return "$id". In schemaNode for child, include "$id":"http://example.com". Then when constructing child, hasId will be true. Then child.findLexicalRoot should return child.

5. testInitializeValidatorsPreloads: verify validator.preloadJsonSchema called once after initializeValidators.

6. testIsDynamicAnchorTrue: schemaNode contains "$recursiveAnchor": true. So when constructing JsonSchema, read method will set dynamicAnchor true. Need to call schema.isDynamicAnchor() returns true.

But read is called later lazily when getValidators invoked; dynamicAnchor set during read. So we need to call getValidators (or initializeValidators) after construction to trigger read. So test: schemaNode = mapper.readTree("{\"$recursiveAnchor\":true}"); then after schema.getValidators() (or initializeValidators), schema.isDynamicAnchor() should be true. Verify.

7. testHasRequiredValidatorAndGetter: schemaNode with "required": [] . In read, requiredValidator set. After getValidators, schema.hasRequiredValidator() true, getRequiredValidator returns validator (same mock). Use verify.

8. testHasTypeValidatorAndGetter: schemaNode with "type":"string". After getValidators, hasTypeValidator true, getTypeValidator returns validator (cast). Since validator is mock of JsonValidator, but code casts to TypeValidator; need to make validator mock be a TypeValidator subclass. We can create a mock TypeValidator.

Create TypeValidator typeValidator = mock(TypeValidator.class); then when(validationContext.newValidator(..., "type", ...)).thenReturn(typeValidator). For other calls return generic validator.

Will need to differentiate based on pname.

We can use Answer to return different validator based on pname.

Simplify: set up validationContext.newValidator to return a mock JsonValidator; for type we also assign to a field.

But getTypeValidator expects a TypeValidator. It will cast; if we return a generic mock that doesn't extend TypeValidator, ClassCastException. So we need a mock that implements both JsonValidator and TypeValidator (TypeValidator extends JsonValidator). So we can mock TypeValidator.

When validationContext.newValidator called with pname "type", return typeValidator; else return generic validator.

We'll use Mockito Answer: when(validationContext.newValidator(...)).thenAnswer(invocation -> { String pname = invocation.getArgument(1); if ("type".equals(pname)) return typeValidator; else return validator; });

Now test.

9. testToString: verify format.

Ok.
